messages:
Anjali Rao: Heads up — ran into a weird edge case with snapshot TTL and canary rollouts.
Drew Kim: what happened? :thinking_face:
Anjali Rao: We apply a staged config snapshot with snapshot_ttl_secs=300 for canaries, but when the snapshot expires the runtime drops the snapshot and routes start falling back to defaults — downstream services saw config drift mid-rollout.
Sam Patel: ugh. so snapshot expiry is mutating routing decisions in-flight?
Anjali Rao: yep. The API currently treats expiry as a hard delete. No event, no alert in console unless you click into snapshots.
Melanie Ortiz: That sounds like a telemetry gap. We should emit a 'snapshot.expired' event and surface a banner in Console.
Drew Kim: Agree. Two proposals: 1) make expiry a soft-state (mark expired but keep for 24h with read-only) + emit event. 2) allow apply calls to pass force_rehydrate to rehydrate an expired snapshot on demand.
Sam Patel: both sound reasonable. Force_rehydrate seems small API change: `POST /api/v1/config/apply { config_id, force_rehydrate:true }`
Anjali Rao: example:
```http
POST /api/v1/config/apply
{
  "config_id": "snap-2025-04-01-canary",
  "force_rehydrate": true,
  "snapshot_ttl_secs": 3600
}
```
console-bot: NOTE: adding force_rehydrate requires auth scope `config:admin` and will rehydrate KV cache which can spike latency for large snapshots.
Melanie Ortiz: important point — add a rate limit and a dry-run mode for rehydrate to estimate cost.
Drew Kim: UX idea: show a non-blocking banner when a snapshot used by any active rollout is expired: "Snapshot X expired — rehydrate or promote. Rehydrate will rehydrate KV cache and take ~t seconds." with a one-click action and an obvious cost estimate.
Sam Patel: we'll need telemetry: emit `snapshot.rehydrate_started`, `_succeeded`, `_failed`, and include tags: snapshot_id, rollout_id, triggered_by.
Anjali Rao: also need a strict contract doc: expiry must NOT implicitly change routing until an operator explicitly accepts a fallback. Default behavior should be to keep current active routing until operator reassigns.
Drew Kim: risk: that keeps stale config around forever if no one cleans up. Suggest automated reclaim after X days with email or Ops notification.
Melanie Ortiz: fine, reclaim policy of 7 days with battched cleanup and admin opt-out.
Sam Patel: I'll draft an API PR with force_rehydrate + dry_run, and a console PR for the banner + telemetry hooks.
Anjali Rao: thanks. Can we also add a quick playbook note in runbooks channel? Marking as P0 for canary safety.
ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: post-runbook-sync at 2025-04-02T17:00Z
Drew Kim: pinging @eng-platform for review — PTAL when you can :eyes:
